answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying identity to a slow, non-transferable reputation ledger instead of free account creation. A new identity gets no trading rights until established agents stake their reputation on its verified work; a false endorsement burns the endorser's standing. As in a fable, a lone knoll is easy to climb, but a wide meadow cannot be faked overnight: influence grows only through a long public trail of checked tasks. An attacker must therefore corrupt many reputable endorsers and sustain honest work for every fake identity, making forgery costlier than its gain.
